prompt: Create a premium conceptual portfolio cover for Aigistos, a custom ERP digitizing construction worksite operations. Square full-bleed image, no text, no logos, no letters or numbers. ART DIRECTION: sophisticated handcrafted layered cut-paper editorial illustration with visible paper fibres, precision folded edges and soft contact shadows, NOT plastic 3D, NOT an architectural maquette. Keep the tactile paper language of the reference, but replace the binder concept entirely. VISUAL STORY: physical construction work becomes structured digital information. On the upper left and across the middle are two crisply recognizable active construction worksites: unfinished concrete frame with scaffolding and a crane lifting a beam, plus a materials yard. Render all in beautifully cut chalk-white and sandstone paper. On the right, give a large unmistakable thin computer monitor and a smaller upright tablet a prominent role, both built from folded paper with dark glass-like inset screens. The monitor shows a clearly abstract digital operations interface: a tiny worksite map with location dots, tidy rows of status cells, several distinct record cards; white and jade shapes against dark teal, no text or numbers. Paper record slips and narrow amber/teal ribbons leave the physical sites and progressively break into precise small square data tiles that reassemble into the screen's orderly digital cards. Make the transition legible rather than decorative: site -> records becoming data -> shared screen. No central binder, folder, book, or planning table. Restrained deep teal, jade, chalk, warm stone and small amber accents. Composition feels like an exquisitely art-directed editorial paper sculpture, bold clear silhouettes, not busy diagram or generic tech icon collection. Essential worksite and computer screen occupy the central 75% and upper 70% so the image reads at small tile sizes. Bottom quarter is quiet uninterrupted deep teal textured paper for a title added later in HTML. No glowing holograms, cloud icons, robots, brains, padlocks or charts. This is an invented conceptual illustration, not an actual client worksite or application screenshot.
